title: Monday After Closing
subject: a woman who winds the eleven antique clocks in a small city museum every Monday after closing, and the one clock she leaves stopped at ten past four on purpose
caption: Dunedin-sound jangle-pop, New Zealand 1980s lo-fi lineage. Two jangling twelve-string-style electric guitars in bright open chords, trebly melodic bass, shuffling snare-and-tom drums, tambourine and a short organ drone in the chorus. Four-track room sound with light tape hiss, unpolished and close. Female lead, plain light alto, slightly ragged but clearly sung, a friend doubling the chorus. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 138 BPM, D major. Bright, wistful mood. No synth, no autotune, no big reverb wash, no distorted fuzz, no drum machine.
lyrics:
[Intro - jangling guitars, tambourine]

[Verse 1]
Monday after the doors are locked
I take the keys and I take the stairs
Eleven clocks in the Long Gallery
Ten brass keys on a loop of string

[Pre-Chorus]
One by one I turn them round
Listen for the tick to settle down

[Chorus]
Ten past four, ten past four
That one I never wind
All the others keep on going
That one stays behind

[Verse 2]
The guard goes home at half past six
The radiator knocks and ticks
The oak one always strikes too late
The tall one swears it's half past eight

[Chorus]
Ten past four, ten past four
That one I never wind
All the others keep on going
That one stays behind

[Bridge - guitars drop to a single strum]
The curator asked me to fix it
That was three years of Mondays ago

[Chorus]
Ten past four, ten past four
That one I never wind
Everybody's racing round the room
It's the one that stays behind

[Outro - jangle fade, tambourine]
Ten past four, ten past four
Lock the door, I'll be back next Monday
